title: Scientific Research Knowledge Assistant Project Progress Report
author: Sergei Iakovlev
description: My project is a local scientific research assistant. A user asks a question about a collection of research papers, and the app retrieves supporting passages, writes an answer and links back to the paper pages. It can help a research team compare methods and inspect evidence. I compare traditional passage search with Graph RAG, which can also follow reviewed connections between papers, methods and datasets. The current product uses prepared five- and twenty-paper collections. M8 will add user-provided papers; it is not available yet.

features.element: Environment setup and locked Python/dependency configuration
Read a research PDF, create searchable passages and generate cited answers
Five-paper pilot, source-bound claim extraction and human review
Four retrieval modes, research workflows, interface and evidence exports
Twenty-paper corpus and original controlled retrieval/answer evaluation
Broader graph routes, shared reranker and exploratory follow-up evaluation
Working local demonstration, source cards, corpus selection and checked downloads
User-provided PDFs/links and dynamic collections: planned, not implemented

completion_basis: Seven of eight technical milestones shown are complete, equally counted; not effort-weighted, answer accuracy or M8 implementation progress.

challenges.detail: PDF reading order, parsed section names and generated wording can be imperfect. I retain exact quotations and PDF page references, and require human review before scientific claims become approved facts. Citation IDs alone do not prove every sentence correct.

Graph retrieval did not add selected evidence on the held-out questions. Broader routes and reranking were tested, but no held-out traversal benefit was established. This remains a reported limitation, not a claimed quality improvement.

The local generator competes for limited memory. Product checks observed answers taking 35-76 seconds, with additional cold-start time possible. CPU embeddings and bounded contexts help manage resources; instantaneous answers are not promised.

Source claims and evaluation annotations needed separate human review. Each study used a small held-out sample and one answer scorer. The follow-up author knew earlier outcomes, so that study is explicitly exploratory.

Earlier corpus/review mismatches and citation-display bugs were fixed and checked. Users still cannot upload their own papers in the UI. The newly planned M8 addresses this through isolated collections, imports, ordinary QA and optional reviewed graph features.
